newsitem.title: PERU: No more releases until talks - Peru rebel spokesman.
newsitem.headline: No more releases until talks - Peru rebel spokesman.

text.p: The international spokesman for Marxist rebels holding 74 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima said on Monday there would be no more releases until the government restarted negotiations.

"There will be no more releases so long as the government fails to agree to a political solution," Isaac Velazco told Reuters. He defined a "political solution" as the "allowing of communication with our imprisoned comrades and the presence at the residence of government negotiator Domingo Palermo to establish points of negotaition."

Negotiations started when Palermo had the first face-to-face meeting Dec. 28 with Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, the rebel leader inside the compound. Velazco said President Alberto Fujimori had broken them off with his subsequent statements.
In a speech on Thursday, Fujimori said the MRTA guerrillas, who he called "terrorists", were bent on pointless violence that only served to increase poverty in Peru.
The rebels have not freed more hostages since New Year's Day. It has been the longest gap between releases in the 20-day siege, during which more than 430 captives have been set free.
"We have made too many gestures. We have released many people without receiving a single response from the government," Velazco said by telephone from Hamburg, Germany.
